qa.q: What is a volcano, and what is volcanicity?
qa.a: A volcano is an opening in the crust through which magma, gases and ash come out. Volcanicity is all the processes by which magma moves towards or onto the surface.
They form at plate margins and at hot spots. Mount Cameroon is on the Cameroon Volcanic Line, inside the African Plate.

qa.q: Is Mount Cameroon active, dormant or extinct? Explain.
qa.a: Mount Cameroon is active, because it has erupted in recent times (1999 and 2000) and can erupt again.

sum.title: I. Meaning and Types of Volcanoes
defs: A volcano is an opening (vent) in the crust through which magma, gases and ash come out onto the surface.
Volcanicity is all the processes by which magma rises into the crust or onto the surface.
items: A. Origin
Volcanoes form at plate margins and at hot spots. In Cameroon, they lie on the Cameroon Volcanic Line: Bioko, Mount Cameroon, Manengouba, Bamboutos and Oku.
cameroon_volcanic_line.png
B. Types by Activity
– Active: it erupts or has erupted in recent history (Mount Cameroon).
– Dormant: it has not erupted for a long time but can erupt again.
– Extinct: it will not erupt again (Mount Manengouba).

qa.q: Study the structure of a volcano.
Name the main parts of a volcano, from the bottom to the top.
qa.a: The main parts are the magma chamber, the vent (pipe), the cone and the crater at the top.

sum.title: II. Structure of a Volcano
sum.intro: A volcano has the following parts:
items: The Main Parts
– Magma chamber: an underground store of molten rock.
– Vent: the pipe through which magma rises.
– Cone: the mountain built of layers of lava and ash.
– Crater: the bowl-shaped hole at the top.
volcano_structure.png

qa.q: What is the difference between intrusive and extrusive features?
qa.a: Intrusive features form when magma cools inside the crust. Extrusive features form when lava and ash cool on the surface.
Dyke (vertical), sill (horizontal), laccolith (dome-shaped) and batholith (very large mass, often of granite).

qa.q: What is the difference between a crater and a caldera?
qa.a: A crater is the small hole at the top of a volcano. A caldera is a very large hollow formed when the top of a volcano collapses after a big eruption.

sum.title: III. Volcanic Features
sum.intro: Magma forms features inside the crust and on the surface:
items: A. Intrusive Features (illustration only)
They form when magma cools inside the crust: dyke, sill, laccolith, lopolith, phacolith, batholith and volcanic plug. We see them after erosion removes the rocks above.
volcano_structure.png
B. Extrusive Features
– Lava cones: gentle slopes of runny lava.
– Ash and cinder cones: steep, small cones of ash.
– Composite cones: layers of lava and ash.
– Craters, calderas and lava plateaus.
– Crater lakes, such as Lake Nyos and the lakes of Manengouba.

evaluation: What is the difference between magma and lava?
Magma is molten rock under the ground; lava is molten rock that has reached the surface.
Give an example of an active volcano in Cameroon.
Mount Cameroon is an active volcano.
A dyke is a vertical wall of magma that cooled inside the crust.
remediation: Molten rock under the ground is ______.
The bowl-shaped hole at the top of a volcano is the ______.
A volcano that will not erupt again is ______.
A horizontal sheet of cooled magma is a ______.
A very large collapsed crater is a ______.
Mount Cameroon lies on the Cameroon Volcanic ______.
end.remediationAnswers: 1. magma 2. crater 3. extinct 4. sill 5. caldera 6. Line

teacherNote: Correction: Mount Cameroon is not at a subduction margin. It is on the Cameroon Volcanic Line, a line of volcanoes inside the African Plate. Its eruptions are mostly quiet flows of basalt lava.
Checked eruptions of Mount Cameroon in the 20th–21st centuries: 1909, 1922, 1954, 1959, 1982, 1999, 2000 (and small activity in 2012). Its height is about 4,040–4,095 m, depending on the survey.
Mount Manengouba is usually described as extinct (dormant for a very long time).
